question: What is the main goal of a School Health Programme?

options.A: To replace family-based healthcare services completely
options.B: To promote and protect the well-being of students and staff
options.C: To generate revenue for school infrastructure
options.D: To provide academic tutoring for struggling students

explanation: Spot on! The heart of any school health program is keeping everyone—both students and staff—physically, mentally, and socially safe and healthy. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T4#GNS225_U4_T4_h1)

question: Why is the active leadership of school management so important for a School Health Programme?

options.A: It allows administrators to practice medicine without a license
options.B: It eliminates the need for professional school nurses
options.C: It ensures that health policies remain strictly confidential
options.D: It provides the administrative backbone needed for proper coordination

explanation: You got it! School leaders have the official power and organization needed to guide and keep health activities running smoothly. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T4#GNS225_U4_T4_h1)

question: Who has the main responsibility for setting health rules that must be followed in a school?
explanation: Exactly! The school management team holds the authority required to create and enforce official health policies. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T4#GNS225_U4_T4_h2)

question: What is a common mistake school administrators make when it comes to health policies?

options.A: Allowing students to write their own safety rules
options.B: Consulting too many medical professionals before acting
options.C: Making policies that are far too simple to understand
options.D: Drafting policies but failing to actually enforce them

explanation: That's right. Writing a great policy on paper won't help if management doesn't follow through and monitor it daily! [learn more](GNS225_U4_T4#GNS225_U4_T4_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a basic facility needed for a healthy school environment?
explanation: Correct! While a big pool is fun, basic health needs are all about clean water, good toilets, and a clinic space to care for sick students. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T4#GNS225_U4_T4_h3)

question: A school suddenly reports many students down with waterborne gastroenteritis. Which management duty failed here?

options.A: Provision of infrastructure and clean water

explanation: Spot on. Waterborne illnesses are a clear warning sign that safe drinking water and proper sanitation need urgent attention. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T4#GNS225_U4_T4_h3)

question: Why must school management set aside specific funds in their yearly budget for health?

options.A: To purchase luxury furniture for administrative offices
options.B: To pay for students' personal family medical bills
options.C: To purchase medical supplies and maintain health facilities

explanation: You nailed it! Having dedicated funds means first-aid items, cleaning products, and clinic tools are always ready when emergencies happen. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T4#GNS225_U4_T4_h4)

question: What is a common error that new administrators make during financial planning?

options.A: Overfunding the school clinic at the expense of classrooms
options.B: Cutting health and sanitation budgets when funds become tight
options.C: Spending all school funds exclusively on medical equipment
options.D: Refusing to accept government grants for school feeding

explanation: Exactly! Unprepared leaders sometimes treat health programs as optional extras, rather than seeing them as totally essential. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T4#GNS225_U4_T4_h4)

question: How does school management help promote health teaching in the classroom?

options.A: By banning discussions about personal hygiene and nutrition
options.B: By ensuring health education is properly timetabled and resourced
options.C: By personally teaching every biology class in the school
options.D: By leaving health teaching entirely up to extracurricular clubs

explanation: Spot on! Management sets up the timetable and supplies the learning materials so teachers can teach health topics effectively. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T4#GNS225_U4_T4_h5)

question: Why is it important to include health topics in the regular school timetable?

options.A: It replaces the need for any physical school infrastructure
options.B: It ensures students spend less time sitting in traditional classrooms
options.C: It guarantees that every student will pursue a career in nursing
options.D: It equips them with lifelong knowledge to prevent illness and make good choices

explanation: Correct! Classroom lessons build health awareness, helping students practice healthy habits long after they leave school. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T4#GNS225_U4_T4_h5)

question: Which outside group is most important for a school to partner with when planning student immunizations?
explanation: You got it! Local health clinics are our go-to partners because they provide the trained staff and vaccines for school immunization drives. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T4#GNS225_U4_T4_h6)

question: What is the biggest advantage of school management partnering with local health authorities?

options.A: Free commercial advertising for the school in the community
options.B: Elimination of all school fees for enrolled students
options.C: Direct control over local government tax policies
options.D: Quick access to public health support during disease outbreaks

explanation: Spot on! Strong community ties mean the school won't have to face sudden health emergencies or disease outbreaks all on its own. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T4#GNS225_U4_T4_h6)

question: What is an important task for school management when evaluating their health programme?

options.A: Reviewing clinic attendance logs to spot health trends
options.B: Changing the academic grading system every term
options.C: Firing teachers who report sick with malaria
options.D: Keeping all student medical records strictly secret from staff

explanation: Exactly! Checking clinic records helps leaders spot recurring health issues early and take quick, smart action. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T4#GNS225_U4_T4_h7)

question: Why must school management regularly inspect food vendors working on school grounds?

options.A: To determine which meals are most popular among the teachers
options.B: To replace the school kitchen staff with professional chefs
options.C: To collect daily taxes from food sellers for the school account
options.D: To prevent foodborne illnesses and ensure high hygiene standards

explanation: Spot on! Routine checks protect everyone on campus from contaminated meals and poor food handling habits. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T4#GNS225_U4_T4_h7)
